Setting.name: SignatureFP
Setting.value:
This rule is designed to protect user information while using the browser to surf untrusted web sites.

It is possible to use the browser to explore the content of the system hard drive and it is possible that in doing so, the user will instruct the browser to open email files in a legitimate way.

The recommended best practice to avoid this type of false positive is to use the web browser only to access web sites and to use Windows Explorer to browse the system hard drive.
If you observe signature triggers or false positives that should be mentioned in this section, please refer to KB67561 in the Trellix Knowledge Base. https://kcm.trellix.com/corporate/index?page=content&id=KB67561

Setting.name: SignatureNotes
Setting.value:
The minimum supported ENS version for this signature is 10.5.3. This event indicates an attempt to read an email file type by Internet Explorer. In most configurations the browser should not access files of this type directly, and such an operation might suggest that the browser is compromised and that an attacker is attempting to use the browser to read private information from the machine running the browser.

The event will trigger each time the browser attempts to open a file whose type is known to be used by Microsoft Outlook. These types include single email files, address book files and personal folder files.

This event will not be triggered if the email file accessed by the browser is located in a directory used for browser operations, such as the windows system directory or the temporary directories used by the browser.

Setting.name: SignatureName
Setting.value: Possible Lambsys Linux Cryptominer Backdoor Detected

Setting.name: SignatureNotes
Setting.value: (Refer to KB article 51504 for details about supported platforms.) This event indicates a possible Lambsys infection. The malware drops hidden staging and watchdog artifacts (procq, init_rmount, /var/tmp/.xlamb/) to persist across reboots, evade detection, and mine Monero. This is associated with MITRE ATT&CK Tactic(s): Impact, Persistence, Defense Evasion and Technique(s): T1496, T1564.001, and T1074.

Setting.name: SignatureFP
Setting.value: Adding programs to the startup list is commonly done by legitimate applications, such as setup programs and anti-virus software, when they are installed or upgraded, so this event may indicate a false positive. If it was caused by a known, legitimate application, create an exception. However, due to the potential for harm, we recommend that questionable instances be thoroughly investigated. If you observe signature triggers or false positives that should be mentioned in this section, please refer to KB67561 in the Trellix Knowledge Base. https://kcm.trellix.com/corporate/index?page=content&id=KB67561

Setting.name: SignatureNotes
Setting.value: The minimum supported ENS version for this signature is 10.5.3. This event indicates that a new program has been designated to run at startup, or that the startup status of an existing program has been modified. This action presents a security risk, as many Trojan horses add themselves to the list of startup programs so that they execute with high privileges at startup (or logon) time.
